analysis.investment_thesis: Equitas SFB is caught in a severe NPA/credit cost cycle — net profit collapsed 82% from INR 799 Cr to INR 147 Cr in FY25, destroying ROE to a dismal 2.42%, while finance costs (29% CAGR) are growing nearly 2x faster than revenue (17% CAGR). At 51x trailing P/E with no promoter holding disclosed, this is not the quality financial franchise I back with conviction.
key_strengths: Revenue scaling well — 17.4% CAGR to INR 4,066 Cr with balance sheet near doubling to INR 52,836 Cr shows franchise is growing
Low P/B of 1.28x means limited downside on book value; strong DII support at 50.87% suggests institutional belief in eventual recovery
Forward P/E of 11.28x implies market expects earnings to bounce back ~4.5x — if MFI/MSME stress normalises, re-rating can be sharp
key_risks: ROE crash to 2.42% is catastrophic for a bank — needs to hit 15%+ before I even consider buying
Finance costs growing at 29% CAGR vs revenue at 17% means NIM compression is structural, not cyclical — this is a serious spread problem
Microfinance/MSME borrower stress (visible in FY25 profit collapse) may persist; MFI-heavy small finance banks are in an industrywide NPA upcycle
red_flags: Net profit down 82% YoY — INR 799 Cr → INR 147 Cr — while total assets kept growing; this is a quality problem, not just a cyclical dip
No promoter shareholding data disclosed — for a bank this is a serious governance transparency concern
Finance cost CAGR of 29.1% outpacing revenue CAGR of 17.4% means every rupee of loan growth is destroying margin — the model is under structural stress
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Equitas SFB sits in a sector I love — financial inclusion banking for India's underserved MSME and microfinance segments — but love for a sector does not override love for numbers. The FY25 numbers are deeply troubling. Net profit of INR 147 Cr on a INR 52,836 Cr asset book translates to ROA of barely 0.28% and ROE of 2.42%. A bank earning 2.42% on equity is not a bank I can own with conviction. The finance cost explosion — from INR 1,421 Cr in FY22 to INR 3,060 Cr in FY25, a 29% CAGR — tells me deposit costs and borrowing costs have risen sharply while the bank's MFI and MSME loan book is suffering delinquencies. Revenue grew 17%, but spreads are being compressed into nothing.

The forward P/E of 11.28x is mathematically intriguing — it implies the street expects INR 660-670 Cr in forward earnings, a near 4.5x recovery from INR 147 Cr. That recovery is theoretically possible if credit costs normalise, but I have seen too many Indian SFBs promise NPA recoveries that never arrived on schedule. I need to see two consecutive quarters of improving asset quality, credit cost below 2.5%, and ROE trending back toward 12-15% before I take a second look. Right now, this is a turnaround story at a speculative price, not the India growth champion I bet on. Watch and wait — do not buy.
